_meta.purpose: Fixed sentences, labels and rules of pipeline/results.py, which writes data/pipeline/results_by_need.json, results_flat.csv and results_summary.json. Nothing in this file is a quote of a NASA document; the quotes are copied by results.py from references.json.
_meta.templates: A template holds no digit. {slot} is replaced by a count of the block; [slot|one|many] prints 'one' if the slot equals 1 and 'many' otherwise. The only text with digits is the label of pile 3, which carries the listing date as the team lead worded it.

order_rule.text: Results are ranked by the conditions their own words state, against the ranges of the environment, with no weights and no assumed values: first the results that state an oxygen and a pressure inside the ranges of the environment; then those that state at least one of its conditions (oxygen, pressure, gravity level) inside its range and none outside; then those that state no oxygen, pressure or gravity level; last those listed for this environment under other conditions. Inside a group: a result whose item is labelled measured (or carries no label) comes before a result labelled computed by the authors, simulation or preliminary (field result_kind of the item, see result_kind); then a result that names a material comes first; then by item id; then in the order of findings.csv. The groups are those of findings_by_environment.json; this file does not place a result again.

groups.label: At the oxygen and pressure of this environment
About one stated condition of this environment
Stated without oxygen, pressure or gravity level
At other stated conditions (not listed for this environment by findings_by_environment.json)

result_kind.note: Field 'result_kind' of a reference item (added 2026-11-15; items added earlier carry none and are ordered as measured). An item whose kind is not measured begins its text with the label of its kind; check U5 verifies it. 'relation' is set for an item whose experiment is not a PSI investigation of this catalogue; such an item has 'investigation' null.

labels.computed_by_authors: Computed by the authors, not a measurement:

units.note: The unit of a printed value is taken from the item's 'values' field 'unit' where it has one; otherwise from the key of the value by the first rule below whose token is in the key (the keys are the team's names for the printed columns; the unit is the unit those names carry). A key that matches no rule has no unit. The rules from flow_cms to he_pct at the head of the list were added on 2026-11-15 for the keys of the items added that day; they leave the unit of every value held before unchanged.

values_rules.rows: A 'rows' list: one printed value per field of a row that is not a row label ('row_label_fields'); the row labels are kept with each value.
values_rules.matrix: An object with one 'columns_*' list and lists of the same length under other keys: one printed value per key and column; the key is the material as printed, the column is printed with its own unit.
values_rules.list: A list under a key that ends in '_range' is one printed value (the range as held); any other list gives one printed value per element.
values_rules.object: An object of plain values: one printed value per key.
values_rules.scalar: A number or a text: one printed value.
values_rules.entry_rows: An entry made from one row of a table (row_source 'rows[i]') takes the values of that row; an entry made from one column of a table (column_of) takes that column; an entry made from element i of a list (row_source 'key[i]') takes element i of that list and of every other top-level list of the item with the same length. An entry with a row but neither takes no printed value ('values_scope' not_split_by_row): the item's values stay in 'items'. An entry without a row takes all values of the item.

labels.criteria: What NASA's documents state as criteria, requirements, definitions and limits for this question
labels.process: Where this question sits in NASA's fire-safety process
labels.unprocessed: In the archive, not in a table
labels.lower_shelf: Not found in the files opened
labels.no_record: No record in PSI (listing of 14 November 2026)
labels.caveats: What the documents say limits these results

sentences.found: Quoted from the documents of the reference list. The grouping and the order are the team's, by a fixed rule on the conditions each statement states; they are not NASA's conclusions. A result is not carried from the condition where it was stated to another one.
sentences.printed_values: Printed values are the numbers of the item exactly as held in references.json, each with the column or quantity it was printed under. The team computes nothing with them.
sentences.criteria: A criterion is quoted next to the results. The team compares nothing with it.
sentences.process: Measures are quoted from NASA documents for the case they describe. The team recommends nothing.
sentences.recorded: Counts of tests in PSI's experimental tables as the team mapped them; the counts are the team's computation, not NASA's.
sentences.unprocessed: A test is recorded, and a value this question needs is not in NASA's table. Listed here: the file groups that name these tests, how many files were opened, and what was read. A listed file group is not shown to hold the value.
sentences.lower_shelf: Not in a table, and no header accepted for it in any file opened so far. This is a statement about the files opened, not about the archive.
sentences.no_record: No test at this condition is in PSI's per-test tables as the team mapped them, on one of the stated grounds, each printed with its source. The statement describes PSI's record on that date.
sentences.caveats: Quoted from the documents of the reference list, in the same groups and order as the results.
sentences.found_all_questions: Results tagged for all questions are listed after the results tagged for this question, in the same groups and order.
sentences.not_research_guidance: A research exploration tool, not safety guidance. Read by an AI agent; not checked by a person.

headline.results: {n_tagged} quoted [n_tagged|result|results] tagged for this question: {n_at} at the oxygen and pressure of this environment, {n_about} about one of its stated conditions, {n_without} stated without these conditions, {n_other} at other stated conditions; {n_with_values} with printed values.
headline.all_questions: {n_general_need} more tagged for all questions: {n_general_at} at the oxygen and pressure of this environment, {n_general_about} about one of its stated conditions.
headline.tests_ranges: {counted} [counted|test|tests] counted, {inside} inside the oxygen and pressure ranges of this environment by recorded values.
headline.tests_no_ranges: {counted} [counted|test|tests] counted; this environment sets no oxygen or pressure range.

audit.number_rule: A number of an item's text or quote is a token of the words that reads as a number (an optional sign, digits, an optional decimal part, an optional '%'), after the punctuation around it is removed. A token joined to letters by a hyphen (HT90-40, 0-g, 5-cm-wide) and a token after one of 'label_words' is a label, not a printed value. A number is 'not in values' if no number held by the item's values equals it.
audit.added_values_topics: Values blocks were added by hand (field 'values_from' = 'item text') only to items without values whose text or quote prints a number about solid-material flammability limits, flame spread rates, extinction conditions, combustion products or smoke particle size, copying the number exactly as printed.

top_five.note: Added 2026-11-15. Rule, templates and fixed sentences of pipeline/results_top.py, which writes data/pipeline/results_top.json and results_top.csv from results_by_need.json. No weights and no scores.
top_five.selection_rule: Take the need's own results (the entries of found.entries, not the ones tagged for all questions). Order them by (1) condition group as in results_by_need.json: at the oxygen and pressure of the environment; about one stated condition; without these conditions stated; other conditions; (2) result_kind: measured (or no label) before computed_by_authors, then simulation, then preliminary; (3) results of a PSI investigation of this catalogue (no 'relation') before results carrying 'relation' (related NASA experiment); (4) results with printed values before results without; (5) item id; ties keep the order of found.entries. Then walk the order and take a result unless two results of the same document are already taken (so at most two per document), until five are taken. If fewer than five exist after the rule, take what exists; the header says how many are shown.
top_five.line_note: The line is the item's team-worded text, whole and unchanged (no cut, whatever its length).
top_five.values_label: The row label, the key under which the printed column or quantity is held and the column, joined by ', ' (empty parts left out); the unit is left out where the value has none; cells are joined by '; '.
top_five.values_more: and {n} more in the source table
top_five.conditions_note: From the finding's conditions: oxygen as '{min}% O2' or '{min} to {max}% O2', pressure as written, gravity level, flow as '{value} cm/s', material as written; a condition not stated is left out; parts joined by '; '.
top_five.header_template: {n} [n|quoted result|quoted results] for this question; showing {k}. {a} at the oxygen and pressure of this environment, {b} about one of its stated conditions.
top_five.no_result: No quoted result is tagged for this question.
top_five.skip_reason: two results of this document already taken
top_five.footer: Quoted from NASA documents with the numbers as printed. Read by an AI agent, not checked by a person. The team compares nothing and recommends nothing.
